page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a-nps1.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 x86_64 processor operating at 2.55 GHz. The configuration features 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supplying 32 dedicated vCPUs. Memory is allocated at 64.0 GB, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio equal to 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth capacity, includes no GPUs, and omits local storage, relying on attached cloud storage volumes.

Performance data places the ecs.c7a-nps1.8xlarge in the upper tier for single-core compute performance, recorded at 2697.59 in stress-ng single-core tests. Its PassMark memory score of 2754.99 also ranks in the top 25% relative to comparable cloud benchmarks. Multi-threaded metrics fall in the middle range across general benchmark suites, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 13194.0, a PassMark CPU score of 38324.48, and static web serving throughput of 23.65 GB/sec. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 83.67 GB/sec, while write operations peak at 48.11 GB/sec.

By maintaining a lean memory-to-vCPU ratio and excluding local storage, the instance maximizes core density for CPU-bound tasks without added overhead for unused RAM or local disk space. This resource balance provides high compute output efficiency for computational workloads. Recommended workload deployments include software compilation, batch processing, static web serving, Redis caching nodes, and multi-threaded data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a-nps1.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores paired with 64.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 core-to-RAM ratio. The server includes 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, omits local storage, and contains no discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core CPU execution alongside high memory performance scores, while multi-core compute and data decompression throughput maintain steady mid-range metrics. The absence of local disk drives keeps infrastructure lean, directing allocation toward pure processing power. This virtual machine is well suited for CPU-heavy tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, Redis key-value workloads, and enterprise batch processing pipelines.
